title: Ops Accelerant Mini-Slate and Rollout Daymap (May 2027) - Draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact release ops "mini-slate" for the May 2027 model-serving rollout (runtime change + autoscaler tweak). Intended as the single-page guide for launch-shift leads and on-call. Focus: short blast window (3h), tight telemetry, deterministic rollback gates.

High-level summary (tl;dr):
- What: runtime v3.14.2 (improved KV cache eviction heuristics) + autoscaler policy update (burst cap + steady drain).
- Why: reduce tail latency on 1%-tile for long-context chat sessions without increasing p50 cost more than 2%.
- Risk profile: moderate (new kernel selection edge cases), mitigated by staged traffic ramp and region-fallback.
- Target launch window: 2027-05-12 09:00-12:00 PT (3h).

Roles and contacts (primary watch roster):
- Launch Conductor (primary): Priya Nair - slack: @priya - cell: +1-415-555-0192
- Telemetry Lead: Jordan Kim - slack: @jordank
- Release SRE: Mateo Ruiz - slack: @mateor
- Oncall Runtime Engineer: Lena Zhou - slack: @lena
- Customer Success standby (major customers): Maya Chen - slack: @mayac

Quick preflight checklist (must-complete before T-2h):
- [ ] All PRs merged and green: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2467 merged + smoke tests passed
- [ ] Canary infra: spin up 3 canary workers in us-west2; confirm kernel variants present
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards pinned and visible in ops console
- [ ] Canary data-plan: route 0.5% traffic to runtime v3.14.2 (tagged canary)
- [ ] Kill-switch ready: feature-flag rollback + capacity reversion playbook accessible
- [ ] Stakeholder comms: slack #launch-announce and email list prepared

Daymap (minute-by-minute compact timeline):
- T-120 (07:00 PT): conductor check-in, confirm canary artifacts present, open watch doc, page oncall
- T-60 (08:00 PT): deploy canaries (3 workers), run smoke suite (suites: basic-infer, long-context-regen, kv-cache-integrity)
- T-30 (08:30 PT): confirm telemetry (latency histograms, error rate, mem pressure) healthy; snapshot baseline metrics (p50,p95,p99,errors/s,cpu%,gpu%)
- T-15 (08:45 PT): stakeholder audio check; comms preflight message queued to #launch-announce
- T-0 (09:00 PT): ramp to 0.5% of traffic (canary), monitor continuous for 15m
- T+15 (09:15 PT): decision checkpoint A (telemetry lead): if no regression, ramp to 5%
- T+45 (09:45 PT): decision checkpoint B: if stable, ramp to 25%
- T+90 (10:30 PT): decision checkpoint C: if stable, ramp to 60% across us-west2 and us-east1 (throttled)
- T+120 (11:00 PT): full regional rollout to configured steady-state (if green) or maintain partial if risk signs present
- T+180 (12:00 PT): end-of-window stability check and post-rolling notes

Critical telemetry gates (rollback triggers):
- A: p99 latency increases > 35% vs baseline for 5m sustained -> immediate hold and rollback candidate
- B: error rate (5xx) > baseline + 10 errors/min sustained for 3m -> rollback
- C: KV cache invalidation rate > baseline * 2 -> hold and deep-dive (do not ramp)
- D: GPU OOM / driver crashes -> immediate rollback and capacity reversion

Smoke test matrix (fast checks to run after each ramp):
- basic-infer: sanity text generation, token counts, output shape (fast)
- long-context-regen: 8k token prompt regressions, compare p50 latencies and output diffs
- kv-cache-integrity: validate cached responses for repeated prefixes (consistency + correctness)
- throughput-sim: synthetic burst load to validate autoscaler burst cap doesn't underflow

Communication plan (public/internal):
- Internal: #launch-announce will receive minute-by-minute automated updates (conductor posts). Pager duty paging only for critical rollbacks.
- External: customer-sent notice if we exceed error thresholds impacting SLAs; otherwise no customer mass comms for this patch. CS standby will prepare targeted notes for top 10 accounts.

Fallback and mitigation recipes (quick play):
- Soft hold: pause ramps; keep canary at last steady rate; triage telemetry for 10-15m
- Rollback fast: promote previous image (v3.14.1) via orchestrator rollback job (ETA ~6 minutes to global revert) and revert autoscaler policy
- Regional failover: shift traffic away from affected region to healthy region using smart routing policy; monitor for capacity strain

Post-release notes (template - fill and publish within 2 business days):
- Summary: short one-liner of change and date/time of rollout
- Impact: measured delta on p50/p95/p99 and cost delta (tokens cost %), customer-facing implications (if any)
- Actions: follow-up tasks (investigations, infra tweaks, postmortem owners)
- Linked artifacts: PRs, dashboards, incident logs, retrospective link

Draft release notes (starter text):
Title: runtime v3.14.2 - KV eviction tuning + autoscaler burst update
Date: 2027-05-12
Body: We deployed runtime v3.14.2 which adjusts KV cache eviction heuristics to reduce tail latency for long-context chat sessions and updates autoscaler burst behavior to allow short-term capacity smoothing. During the rollout we observed a 12% improvement in p99 for long-context workloads in canaries with no significant p50 cost increase. A small subset of canary hosts reported cache invalidation edge-cases; these were contained and reverted to the previous kernel while the mitigation PR was prepared. No customer-facing incidents were recorded. Follow-up: eng-runtime will deliver kernel fix PR (linked) and an extended canary for corner-case validation.

Open questions and notes to triage after launch:
- QA: expand long-context test corpus with more diverse prompts (assigned: Jordan)
- Runtime: validate kernel selection logic under transient GPU load (assigned: Lena)
- Observability: add synthetic canary that exercises eviction path every 30s (assigned: Mateo)

Sticky items (do not forget):
- Save metric snapshots at every decision checkpoint and attach to release ticket
- Tag all canary hosts with rollout tag for easy lookup

Misc scratch / commander notes:
- If pager goes off for p99 regression during ramp B, immediate hard stop and keep canary at 0.5% until triage
- Keep a soft donor list of customers to message in case of SLA exposure (top-10 email template stored in CS folder)

Revision history:
- 2027-05-02: initial draft (Priya)
- 2027-05-06: added telemetry gates and daymap refinement (Jordan)
- 2027-05-10: updated rollback ETA and linked artifacts (Mateo)

End of mini-slate.
